settings.heading: A small atelier, six generations in.
settings.subheading: Orlaven began in a single workshop on Via degli Artigiani in Torino. Leandro Orlaven, a fourth-generation cutter, wanted to build a jacket that could be repaired, not replaced. Today his grandchildren run the same benches, press the same hides, and sign the same labels.
settings.quote: Every Orlaven jacket is cut, stitched, and finished by one artisan from start to finish.
settings.author: Leandro Orlaven, founder

settings.heading: A short history
settings.subheading: Four decades, one workshop, one obsession: a jacket made well.

settings.heading: 1987 — Beginnings
settings.text: Leandro opens the first Orlaven workshop in Torino with one cutter and two sewers.

settings.heading: 2001 — The first capsule
settings.text: Orlaven releases its signature Biker cut, the beginning of what is now our core line.

settings.heading: 2015 — Lifetime repairs
settings.text: We formalize our lifetime repair guarantee. Jackets bought in the eighties still come home for service.

settings.heading: 2024 — The atelier today
settings.text: Six generations in, we ship worldwide, still from the same Torino workshop.

settings.heading: No corners cut.
settings.subheading: Full-grain hides, solid brass hardware, cotton-silk linings. We choose every component for feel and longevity.

settings.heading: Full-grain bridle leather
settings.description: Aniline-finished, vegetable-tanned hides from a single Tuscan tannery. Patinas rather than fades.

settings.heading: Merino shearling
settings.description: Dense Spanish merino, cured for warmth and combed for softness. Natural insulation, nothing synthetic.

settings.heading: Solid brass hardware
settings.description: Never plated, never hollow. The same brass zips we used in 1987 still open smoothly today.
